messages:
jordan: heads up — canary routing landed but we still need a plan for request/response logging while debugging. we can't enable full payload capture in prod without a redaction+samp strategy. thoughts?

priya: agree. two constraints: 1) devs need enough context to reproduce routing problems (full prompt + response snippets), 2) legal/privacy says no raw PII in logs for hosted customers.

sam: +1. proposal draft: deterministic trace sampling by customer_id (HMAC(project_key, customer_id) % 100 < sample_pct) so we get stable coverage per customer. then apply layered redaction: structural scrubber -> regex scrubber -> heuristics (cc, emails, phones).

lee: how do we handle debugging a specific request that was dropped by routing? if it's sampled out we lose signal. maybe allow on-demand capture via temporary trace-ids (console toggle) that store raw for 24h with strict access logs.

ashley: product note: console toggle should be auditable and limited to SRE/SEs for the tenant. sales will push for developer self-serve but we need consent/notice.

priya: implementation details: 3 log levels — metrics-only (no payload), scrubbed-trace (sanitized JSON with redactions), raw-debug (full payload for on-call). default is scrubbed-trace. scrubbed-trace rules: mask email local parts, replace digits in CC/SSN patterns with X, truncate long strings > 200 chars, remove authorization headers.

sam: regex examples (we'll maintain in config):
```
email: (?<=).+?@[^\s@]+  # simplified, we actually use tokenization + heuristics
cc: (?:4[0-9]{12}(?:[0-9]{3})?|5[1-5][0-9]{14})  # visa/mastercard patterns + Luhn check
phone: (?:\+?\d[\d\-\s]{7,}\d)
```
these are fallbacks; prefer a small ML model to detect named entities for free-form prompts.

jordan: question: do we store the redaction map? i.e., when we replace emails with <EMAIL_1> across a trace, do we keep a reversible mapping? security says reversible maps are bad.

security-bot: @sam @jordan company policy: never store reversible tokens for hosted logs. For Dedicated / Private, reversible mapping may be allowed if customer provides KMS and explicit consent. Audit trail required.

sam: ok so we use per-trace non-reversible placeholders: <EMAIL>, <PHONE>, <CC>, with counts if needed ("<EMAIL x2>"). For debugging handoffs we can export redacted traces.

lee: retention: scrubbed traces 90 days for dedicated customers, 30 days for hosted. raw-debug artifacts 24h and then auto-delete unless ticket created. is that reasonable?

priya: i prefer 60/14/24 to be conservative: 60 days scrubbed for dedicated, 14 for hosted, raw 24h. we should align with GDPR data minimization.

ashley: UX for rollouts: console should surface sampling rate and effective coverage (example: "1% deterministic sampling by customer_id covers ~10% of active customers"). also show last sampled trace timestamp per customer.

jordan: routing-specific: when requests are routed to fallback model, we should tag traces with routing_decision and why (capacity/fallback/latency) — that can be non-PII.

sam: logging knobs per env:
- hosted: sampling default 1% deterministic, scrubbed-trace default
- dedicated: sampling default 5%, option to increase to 100% within tenant settings (compliance dependent)

priya: console feature: "just-in-time capture" — click to enable raw-debug for a single trace-id; causes signed access token audit entry and 24h TTL. must be approved by owner if cross-team.

lee: perf concerns: scrubber must stream — do structural JSON mask while we stream tokens to avoid buffering huge prompts. also ensure KV cache keys are not logged (they often contain prompt prefixes).

sam: good point. we should treat known fields as sensitive by schema: user_message, system_message, tool_outputs. For unknowns, run NER and regex pipeline.

jordan: question for security: can we lean on hashing for identifiers? e.g., store user_id hashed with per-tenant salt so we can correlate traces without seeing real IDs.

security-bot: yes — use HMAC with tenant-scoped key stored in KMS. For hosted, use tenant-specific derived key non-reversible by us. Document the derivation and rotation policy.

ashley: one more product ask: add a per-route telemetry privacy indicator (public|restricted|private) so teams know which routes can include more context when toggled.

priya: next steps: I'll open an RFC with: sampling algorithm, scrubber rules (config + examples), retention matrix, console UI mocks for toggle + audit, and RBAC requirements. @sam @lee please add redaction regex and perf notes to the RFC.

sam: will do, i'll attach test corpus and a small NER model eval.

lee: i'll prototype streaming scrubber and bench on big prompts.

jordan: thanks everyone. tagging @security-bot for final policy sign-off once RFC lands. :thumbsup:
